name: Retro TV Canonical Default Network v3
notes: Canonical channel-plan manifest for Retro TV.
000 is reserved and disabled; it is not a broadcast channel and must tune as No channel.
001-999 is the canonical default broadcast namespace.
1000 is a reserved boundary and is not allocated.
User-imported and user-created television begins at 1001 and may continue beyond four digits.
Protected legacy channels 001-060 must be reconciled non-destructively with the existing working catalogue.
Channel 101 Late Feature is also protected as an existing working Stage 2/3 channel.
Channel identity is separate from programme sources, source availability, and media rights.
Official/source-branded channels require separately verified lawful sources before playback.
Live-preferred channels may use verified official or authorised live sources, with recorded/generated fallback.
No source URL, external ID, live endpoint, or media right is implied merely by a channel identity.
BBC services are intentionally excluded from the default catalogue as a product choice.
Sports paywalled services must not be treated as freely embeddable sources.
Channels 590-599 are reserved for VEVO-oriented music television.
Channels 850-879 are reserved for Live World / webcams.
Channels 900-949 are News / Current Affairs / Information.
The deterministic broadcast clock remains authoritative for schedules; live sources join live rather than seeking into a recording.
